subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Venice: Europe's Gateway
description: Learn Venice: Europe's Gateway in one minute.

hook.text: Venetian traders were the first Europeans to import coffee beans, around 1600.

buildup.text: Venice's merchant ships brought spices, silk, and now coffee from Ottoman ports.

discovery.text: Catholic priests called coffee 'Satan's drink' and petitioned Pope Clement VIII to ban it.

twist.text: The Pope tasted it, loved it, and reportedly said 'We should baptize it.' Coffee was approved.

climax.text: Venice opened Italy's first coffeehouse in 1629. By 1683, Caffè Florian in St. Mark's Square became legendary.

punchline.text: The Pope blessed Satan's drink. Europe was hooked.

quiz.question: What did Pope Clement VIII reportedly say about coffee?
